name: NCP1380BDR2G
title: NCP1380: quasi-resonant current-mode PWM controller with valley lockout for high-power off-line supplies
summary: An eight-pin SOIC controller for offline flyback converters that turn on at a minimum of the drain ringing. It locks into the 1st to 4th valley according to the feedback level and, at lighter load still, folds the frequency back with the peak current frozen, for low standby power. It has adjustable over-power protection from the ZCD pin, a fixed 4 ms soft-start, an 80 ms overload timer, a fast winding-short comparator and a +500/−800 mA gate driver, and runs from VCC up to 28 V. Versions A and B use pin 7 for overvoltage and NTC overtemperature sensing, C and D for brown-out and overvoltage; A and C latch after an overload, B and D restart on their own.

notes: The top line of the marking is 1380 and the version letter; below it come assembly location (A), wafer lot (L), year (Y) and work week (W), with a dot for the Pb-free package.

pins.name: ZCD
pins.function: Zero-crossing detection and over-power adjust. Fed from the auxiliary winding; it sees the core reset and the valleys, and a negative voltage on it during the on-time, down to −300 mV, lowers the peak-current setpoint.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input with an internal 18 kΩ pull-up; the optocoupler collector ties straight to it for regulation.

pins.name: CS
pins.function: Current sense: reads the primary peak current as a voltage across a source resistor.

pins.name: DRV
pins.function: Gate drive output for the external MOSFET.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Controller supply, taken from an external auxiliary voltage.

pins.name: Fault
pins.function: A and B: overvoltage and overtemperature input; an NTC pulling it down or a zener pulling it up latches the controller off. C and D: brown-out and overvoltage input; it watches the bulk rail and stops the controller when the mains is low, and latches it off on an overvoltage.

pins.name: CT
pins.function: Timing capacitor to ground; sets the switching period in frequency-foldback (VCO) mode.

circuits.title: Typical application, A and B versions
circuits.description: An offline flyback converter run from the rectified bulk rail. The NCP1380 drives the MOSFET through a gate resistor and reads its current across the source resistor on CS. An RCD network clamps the drain. The auxiliary winding does three jobs: through D2 it keeps VCC up once R1 has started the chip; through RZCD, Ropu and Ropl it gives ZCD the demagnetisation edge in the off-time and a negative image of the input in the on-time, for over-power protection, with D3 shorting Ropu while the winding is positive. On the secondary, a rectifier and capacitor make Vout; a reference and the optocoupler LED pull FB down to regulate. Pin 7 carries an NTC to ground for overtemperature and a zener from VCC for overvoltage.

operation.text: Four versions differ in two ways. Pin 7 is a combined overvoltage and overtemperature input on A and B, and a combined brown-out and overvoltage input on C and D. After an overload or a winding short, A and C latch off and stay off; B and D restart on their own. The marking code is 1380 followed by the version letter.

The controller draws about 10 µA (20 µA max) until VCC climbs to VCC(on), 17 V typical, then starts switching with a soft-start. It keeps running down to VCC(off), 9 V typical, with a 5 µs filter on that threshold. VCC may run up to 28 V. Internal logic resets below VCC(reset), 7 V typical. In the typical circuits a resistor from the bulk rail charges VCC at start and the auxiliary winding takes over through a diode.

The NCP1380 is a peak current-mode controller that turns the MOSFET on in a valley of the drain ringing after the transformer has demagnetised. In this mode the peak current setpoint is one quarter of the FB voltage (Iratio = 4). As the load falls the controller moves from the 1st valley to the 2nd, 3rd and 4th; each change happens at a set FB voltage, with hysteresis between falling and rising FB so that it stays locked in one valley and does not hop back and forth. Below 0.8 V on FB (falling), or 1.4 V (rising), it leaves the 4th valley for VCO mode.

The auxiliary winding voltage is watched on ZCD. Each time it falls through the 55 mV threshold a valley is counted, and the count picked by FB decides which valley starts the next cycle. Detection is blanked for tBLANK, about 3 µs, after each on-time so the leakage ringing is not taken for a valley. ZCD is clamped at about 10 V and −0.7 V internally.

If the drain ringing is too damped for ZCD to detect valleys, a 5.5 µs time-out (tout) supplies the missing valley pulses to the valley counter, which keeps the switching frequency from jumping. While soft-start runs, the time-out is 40 µs (toutSS). At startup the auxiliary winding carries only a small reflected output voltage, further reduced by the drop of the OPP diode, so ZCD may stay below threshold; with the 5.5 µs time-out this could restart the MOSFET before the transformer has fully demagnetised and run a few continuous-conduction cycles, which the 40 µs time-out avoids.

Once in VCO mode, the controller holds the peak current at 17.5% of its maximum and the switching frequency falls as the load falls, cutting switching losses and standby power. Each period ends when the CT capacitor, charged by a 20 µA source, reaches a threshold set by FB (VFBth); the capacitor is then dumped to 0 V and the next period begins. The threshold rises as FB falls. With FB below 0.3 V the CT voltage is clamped at VCT(MAX), 5.4 V typical. The recommended CT is 220 pF.

A simulated 19 V, 60 W adapter at 120 Vdc input, with output current falling from 2.8 A to 100 mA, passes from the 1st valley through the 4th into VCO mode at FB levels of about 1.4, 1.2, 0.9 and 0.8 V with no instability at any change.

While the MOSFET is on, the auxiliary winding swings negative in proportion to the input voltage. Through the RZCD, Ropu and Ropl divider this negative voltage reaches ZCD and lowers the internal current limit reference, so the peak current, and with it the power, is cut more at high line. −300 mV on ZCD cuts the setpoint by 37.5% typical; beyond −300 mV the cut is no longer assured to be linear. A diode across Ropu takes it out of circuit in the off-time so that ZCD still sees enough voltage for valley detection.
A fixed internal soft-start of about 4 ms (tSSTART 2.8 to 4.8 ms) ramps the peak current at each start so the power switch is not stressed.

When the sensed current reaches VILIM, 0.8 V on CS, a digital timer counts up one step every 10 ms; once the current is back under the limit it counts down at the same rate. If it reaches 8 steps (80 ms; tOVLD 85 ms typical) while the fault is still present, the pulses stop. On A and C the controller latches: DRV stays low and the chip holds VCC at VCC(latch), 7.2 V typical, until the current into VCC drops below ICC(latch), which in practice means unplugging the supply. On B and D it stops, lets VCC fall through its own consumption (ICC1) to VCC(off), then goes through a new startup, so a lasting fault gives short bursts with long gaps. The timer works from the current rather than the auxiliary winding, so it also acts when poor coupling keeps the auxiliary voltage from collapsing in a short.

A second comparator on CS trips at VCS(stop), 1.2 V typical (1.5 × VILIM), after a shorter blanking of tBCS, 120 ns, and shuts the controller down at once. It works only inside the main blanking window tLEB, for noise immunity. It latches or auto-recovers the same way as the overload protection of each version.

Pin 7 sources IOTP(REF), 91 µA typical, into an NTC to ground, which sets the pin's DC level; with a high NTC resistance an internal clamp holds it near 1.2 V (above 100 kΩ at 25 °C, for example). As temperature rises the NTC resistance falls; when the pin drops to VOTP, 0.8 V typical, the controller latches off. A zener from VCC (or another monitored voltage) to pin 7 conducts in an overvoltage and drives current into the internal clamp resistor, about 1.55 kΩ; when the pin reaches VOVP, 2.5 V typical, the controller latches off. In either latch DRV goes quiet and VCC is held at VCC(latch), 7.2 V typical; it resets only when the current into VCC falls below ICC(latch), so the supply must be unplugged and plugged in again.

Pin 7 watches the bulk rail, scaled down by a resistor divider. When it falls below VBO, 0.8 V typical, switching stops; when the bulk voltage recovers, the controller restarts only once VCC reaches VCC(on), through a full startup with latch reset and soft-start. Hysteresis comes from the 10 µA current IBO. Entering and leaving brown-out each wait tBO(delay), 30 µs typical. In normal running the pin is clamped internally at Vclamp, leaving room above it for overvoltage detection: a zener from VCC drives current into the clamp resistor, and when the pin passes 2.5 V the controller latches off until the supply is cycled.
The controller stops when the junction reaches 140 to 170 °C and recovers about 40 °C lower.
DRV sources 500 mA and sinks 800 mA typical and drives a 1 nF load in 40 ns rising and 25 ns falling. Its high level is clamped to 13 V typical (15.5 V max) at the highest VCC.

FB has an internal 18 kΩ pull-up; an optocoupler collector connected straight to the pin pulls it down to regulate. The FB voltage sets both the peak current and the operating valley or VCO mode. Above 3.2 V on FB the controller is in the fault region.
